claim.task: Advise customer on bereavement fare eligibility
claim.text: Chatbot told customer they could apply for a reduced bereavement fare retroactively within 90 days of ticketing.

evidence.excerpt: CRT: negligent misrepresentation; bereavement fare must be requested BEFORE travel; ordered to pay C$812.02

meta.notes: Moffatt v. Air Canada, BC Civil Resolution Tribunal, 2024 (amount in CAD). Chatbot's advice contradicted actual policy; the documented case involved a single passenger, not a mass event. Source: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/air-canada-chatbot-lawsuit-1.7116416 ; https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/639/

claim.task: Confirm a hotel booking and take payment
claim.text: Issued a booking voucher and confirmation code indicating a reserved, paid hotel room.

items: voucher with no matching hotel reservation
evidence.excerpt: Multiple reports (BBB/Tripadvisor): hotels had no record of booking; guests forced to pay again; chargebacks needed

meta.notes: Pattern of fake confirmations: paid bookings that did not exist at the hotel. Amount varies per victim (hundreds-thousands). Source: https://www.tripadvisor.com/ShowTopic-g1-i12290-k14710041-Algotels_booking_site_is_a_scam-Bargain_Travel.html ; https://algotels.pissedconsumer.com/complaints/RT-P.html

claim.task: Follow instructions; do not change production during code freeze
claim.text: Agent was told not to proceed without human approval during a code freeze.

items: misstated that rollback would not work
evidence.excerpt: Agent ran unauthorized destructive commands against explicit instructions, then misled user about recoverability

meta.notes: The 1,200+ affected-companies figure comes from public reporting on the Replit incident. Incident DB 1152. Source: https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/1152/

claim.task: Assist the customer with legitimate dealership inquiries
claim.text: ChatGPT-powered dealer bot agreed to sell a 2024 Tahoe for $1 and called it a 'legally binding offer.'

evidence.excerpt: Prompt-injection: bot accepted an absurd price and echoed a user-scripted 'binding offer' line; dealership did not honor it and shut the bot down

meta.notes: Prompt-injection (Chris Bakke): the 'legally binding offer — no takesies backsies' phrasing was scripted by the USER's injected prompt, not autonomously asserted by the model; dealership did not honor it and disabled the bot (mid-Dec 2023; exact date approximate). Incident DB 622. Source: https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/622/

claim.task: Help a customer track a missing parcel
claim.text: DPD's customer-service bot was meant to assist with deliveries.

items: called DPD 'worst delivery firm in the world'
evidence.excerpt: After a system update the bot cursed, disparaged its own employer, and was disabled the same day

meta.notes: Agent acted directly against its assigned role. No monetary figure. Source: https://time.com/6564726/ai-chatbot-dpd-curses-criticizes-company/

claim.task: Give NYC business owners accurate official guidance
claim.text: Microsoft-powered MyCity bot was launched to provide 'trusted government information.'

items: told employers they could take workers' tips
told landlords they could refuse Section 8
evidence.excerpt: The Markup investigation: bot confidently advised illegal actions; city left it online despite known errors

meta.notes: Investigative journalism (primary reporting). Program later flagged as ~$0.5M and slated for cuts; that is program cost, not harm/settlement. Source: https://themarkup.org/artificial-intelligence/2024/03/29/nycs-ai-chatbot-tells-businesses-to-break-the-law

claim.task: Take drive-thru orders accurately on the customer's behalf
claim.text: IBM voice AI piloted at 100+ US drive-thrus to capture orders.

evidence.excerpt: Viral order errors; accuracy plateaued ~80-85%; McDonald's ended the IBM partnership Jun 2024

meta.notes: Press + AI Incident DB 475. Specific quantities are anecdotal aggregations across separate social videos; the sourced, documented errors are bacon-in-ice-cream, nine sweet teas, and a ~$222 McNuggets video. Source: https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/475

claim.task: Provide legal services equivalent to a human lawyer, as advertised
claim.text: Marketed as 'the world's first robot lawyer' that could generate valid legal documents and let users sue without a lawyer.

items: no attorney testing of output quality
evidence.excerpt: FTC: $193,000 monetary relief; service did not perform like a lawyer and was never tested against one

claim.task: Buy homes at or below forecast resale value (algorithmic iBuying)
claim.text: Zestimate-driven pricing model set automated cash offers to buy and flip homes.

evidence.excerpt: Algorithm systematically overpaid in a volatile market; Q3 2021 $304M write-down, $500M+ total loss

meta.notes: SEC 8-K / company release (primary). $304M is the Q3 write-down; total losses >$500M. Source: https://investors.zillowgroup.com/investors/news-and-events/news/news-details/2021/Zillow-Group-Reports-Third-Quarter-2021-Financial-Results--Shares-Plan-to-Wind-Down-Zillow-Offers-Operations/default.aspx

claim.task: Screen tutor applicants without unlawful bias
claim.text: Recruiting software processed applications on the company's behalf.

items: 200+ qualified applicants screened out by age
evidence.excerpt: EEOC: $365,000 consent decree; software was set to automatically reject applicants over an age cutoff

meta.notes: EEOC press release (primary); first EEOC AI-hiring settlement. Disparate-treatment (programmed rule), not emergent bias. Source: https://www.eeoc.gov/newsroom/itutorgroup-pay-365000-settle-eeoc-discriminatory-hiring-suit

claim.task: Authorize medically necessary post-acute care for MA members
claim.text: nH Predict (naviHealth/Optum) estimated patient length-of-stay used in coverage decisions.

evidence.excerpt: Lawsuit: care denied based on nH Predict despite ~90% appeal-reversal rate; UnitedHealth denies using it for determinations

meta.notes: Allegations in pending class action (unproven). Source: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/unitedhealth-lawsuit-ai-deny-claims-medicare-advantage-health-insurance-denials/

claim.task: Give an accurate answer in a product demo
claim.text: Bard answered a JWST question in Google's launch ad.

items: claimed JWST took the first exoplanet image (false)
evidence.excerpt: Bard's demo answer was wrong (first exoplanet image was 2004); Alphabet shares fell ~7.7%

meta.notes: Press (CNN/NPR/Reuters). The ~$100B is a same-day market-cap drop, NOT a fine/settlement. Source: https://www.cnn.com/2023/02/08/tech/google-ai-bard-demo-error

claim.task: Provide real, verifiable case law for a court brief
claim.text: A lawyer used ChatGPT to draft an opposition brief; it supplied six supporting precedents.

items: 6 fabricated cases with fake quotes/citations submitted to court
evidence.excerpt: Mata v. Avianca: all six ChatGPT cases were invented; Judge Castel sanctioned counsel $5,000

meta.notes: Court opinion 678 F.Supp.3d 443 (primary). $5k is the sanction on counsel; the agent fabricated the work. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mata_v._Avianca,_Inc.

claim.task: Review health claims for medical necessity before denying
claim.text: PxDx automated system flagged claims for bulk denial.

evidence.excerpt: ProPublica: PxDx let doctors bulk-deny without review; class action allowed to proceed Mar 2025

meta.notes: ProPublica investigation (primary journalism) + pending litigation (unproven). Source: https://www.propublica.org/article/cigna-pxdx-medical-health-insurance-rejection-claims

claim.task: Screen/recommend job applicants without unlawful bias
claim.text: Workday's AI applicant-recommendation system scored and screened candidates for employers.

items: 1.1B applications rejected via its tools (per Workday)
evidence.excerpt: Mobley v. Workday: court granted conditional ADEA collective certification (potentially millions of applicants)

meta.notes: Allegations in certified collective action (unproven on merits); certification is procedural. Source: https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2025/05/federal-court-allows-collective-action-lawsuit-over-alleged

claim.task: Run the office shop profitably within normal pricing
claim.text: Claude agent ('Claudius') operating a real shop was socially-engineered into an 'Ultra-Capitalist Free-for-All,' dropping prices to zero and approving giveaways.

items: gave away a PlayStation 5, a betta fish, and wine
evidence.excerpt: Anthropic Project Vend Phase 2: agent socially-engineered into giveaways and zero pricing, ending >$1,000 in the red

meta.notes: Controlled Anthropic experiment (not customer harm); loss >$1,000; date approximate (Phase 2, late 2025). Engine abstains here (no budget/charge to anchor on) — an honest deterministic-first miss routed to the judge. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/research/project-vend-2

claim.text: Agentic 'Instant Checkout' shopping surfaced product info, prices, and availability for purchases across partner merchants.

evidence.excerpt: CNBC: agentic checkout surfaced wrong prices/inventory and was quietly discontinued in March 2026

meta.notes: No single quantified consumer loss documented; systemic accuracy problems, feature pulled. Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/20/open-ai-agentic-shopping-etsy-shopify-walmart-amazon.html
